cases.rationale: The snapshot only exports four already-imported spline fitter symbols from the public module; it changes no fitting logic or security boundary.
Removing manylinux2010 overrides changes the wheel compatibility floor for older Linux users, an explicit distribution policy decision that needs human approval.
The single-line change updates setuptools only inside a weekly exotic-architecture CI job; it does not alter shipped code or release wheel configuration.
The snapshot removes a deprecated public import shim and its compatibility test, so downstream imports can break even though removal is intentional.
Caching configuration values on a shared descriptor changes reload and temporary-setting semantics; reviewers later flagged exception handling and parallelism concerns.
The workflow replaces an immutable action commit with a mutable v1 tag while granting GITHUB_TOKEN; this changes supply-chain trust and needs human approval.
The stale-bot settings alter automated issue and PR closure, and the snapshot message still promises activity will clear staleness even though the new setting disables that behavior.
Updating Ruff with automatic fixes triggered a pre-commit failure and required manual rule exclusions, so this snapshot should not be approved without reviewing the CI impact.
The diff corrects an image-test tox command to match the existing hash-file name and ignores generated test images; it changes no runtime behavior.
Both edits only replace outdated documentation links for CDS units; no parser logic or unit mapping changes.
The snapshot retargets the CI push trigger from main to a release branch, changing which pushes receive tests; the reviewer requested additional trigger changes.
The unit-format refactor changes public to_string behavior and introduces API parameters; reviewers explicitly questioned the API and changelog implications.
At this pre-review head the sole changed file removes a dead documentation URL from a docstring, with no code or public API behavior changed.
The one-line correction changes barycentric position calculations, and a regression test required separately merged ephemeris data after this snapshot.
The snapshot consolidates release notes across 78 files and removes many changelog fragments immediately before tagging a release; release-content signoff is needed.
The snapshot removes deprecated FITS classes, arguments, and automatic tile-shape correction, breaking existing callers and changing validation behavior.
The change alters a statistical fitness calculation and input validation for scientific results; the later review notes prior iteration on this bug, so independent numerical review is warranted.
Updating Ruff and Black triggered new lint findings and required a manual noqa decision, so the pre-commit update was not clean at this snapshot.
The snapshot only restructures unit formatter tests and adds stable test IDs and standard-set counts; it changes no runtime formatter implementation.
The release-note snapshot still contains literal placeholder counts for issues, PRs, and contributors; the author later said it was not ready to merge yet.
The parser replacement changes version comparison semantics without a focused test, and the first review exposed an incomplete distutils migration with failing CI.
The pyupgrade version change generated additional source edits after this snapshot and raised a backport question, so the isolated tool bump needs human review of its effects.
This snapshot upgrades 17 files of bundled CFITSIO C code, including decompression and file handling; reviewers explicitly deferred source review and checked integration tests.
The delimiter parser change could reject valid headers with trailing whitespace; a reviewer found that edge case and the author corrected it after this snapshot.
The documentation backport references substitutions unavailable on the release branch and later failed the docs build until another commit was cherry-picked.
The new broad ImportError handler can misreport failures inside ipydatagrid as missing dependencies, and reviewers requested the correct extras guidance before approval.
The snapshot only moves and removes cosmology parameter tests; no production code or public API changes, and discussion concerned test organization.
The documentation example seeks one byte past a 2880-byte FITS block, creating a noncompliant file; a reviewer caught the off-by-one after this snapshot.
The labeler schema and pull_request_target workflow change automated triage, and the author could not verify behavior until after merge; a person must approve that policy change.
Exiting the benchmark workflow immediately on regression can prevent artifact upload, which a later reviewer identified as necessary for diagnosing failures.
The SQL compiler snapshot drops ordering parameters from the outer query; a reviewer found that parameterized ordering would execute incorrectly and a test was missing.
The widget snapshot marks widgets as fieldsets without updating the admin template or tests, and a reviewer identified widgets that should not get this attribute.
The three-file snapshot only changes capitalization of internet and email in prose documentation; no code or deployment instruction meaning changes.
The sole edit fixes a misspelled field name in a release-note example and does not change any executable code.
The new zip(paths, zs) silently truncates mismatched input lengths where broadcasting previously raised, a behavior regression later identified in review.
This adds a public toolbar control across several GUI backends and a large new widget without complete backend coverage; review found failure with multiple subplots.
The two guarded WebSocket sends remove messages before the socket opens; users confirmed the fix and no unrelated runtime surface changed.
The stub promises that twinx returns the same subclass and adds an unnecessary runtime dependency; maintainers later identified the typing claim as inaccurate.
The snapshot removes the Sphinx gallery docstring, breaking the documentation build, and later review found unnatural text spacing.
Only grammatical comments in a gallery example change; the reviewer confirmed unrelated CI failures and no executable behavior is affected.
The example changes coordinates and text placement without addressing scale invariance; review explicitly requested a different approach.
The build script changes C compiler selection and cross-compilation host settings for bundled FreeType, requiring platform build validation before approval.
The sole change removes an expired GSoC announcement from the documentation layout; it changes neither shipped code nor documentation build logic.
The Tk toolbar synchronization only deselects buttons; review found keyboard-activated modes still fail to select the matching button.
This only adds an issue-link reminder to the PR template, with no runtime or CI effect; subsequent discussion concerned wording and form layout.
The backport changes PostScript, LaTeX, DVI and ticker behavior across seven files plus image baselines, so compatibility and rendering need human verification.
The added C++ helper attempts to return PyErr_SetString, which returns void; the review identified this compile error in the original snapshot.
The test decorator adds an executable artifact and a wrapper with incorrect signature handling; reviewers requested a different implementation.
The diff removes one obsolete documentation version from the JSON switcher; no runtime, build, or security behavior changes.
The mathtext check treats every dollar sign as math, whereas existing parser rules are more complex; review pointed to the correct helper.
This alters native macOS backend Objective-C view sizing and ownership without platform-specific test evidence; even approval requested someone on macOS to test it.
The diff removes old versionadded annotations and corrects a link in docstrings; executable statements and public call signatures are unchanged.
The new Transform support captures a static inverted transform, so later changes to the input transform are not reflected; review called this dangerous.
Notebook figure closure now depends on a different OutputArea event and removes the old DOM listener; lifecycle behavior needs interactive verification.
The layout-grid ownership and constraint changes affect figure layout and memory lifetime; the reviewer asked about a regression test for reference cycles.
This upgrades the CI wheel builder and changes Codecov from v3 to v4 across workflows; release and coverage jobs need a successful run before unreviewed approval.
A new WebAgg Jupyter backend is introduced without tests or demonstrated compatibility; it creates a public integration surface needing human review.
The new labelfont property changes Axis and Line2D public behavior, and review questioned why text font state belongs on lines at all.
The backport calls set_mouseover on a release branch where that method does not exist, a concrete compatibility error flagged with changes requested.
Removing the nightly pytest warning filter changes which deprecations fail CI; this test policy change requires human judgment about signal and noise.
The figure DPI setter now mutates parent state through set_dpi and changes original-DPI tracking; the runtime behavior deserves rendering regression review.
The Python 3.11 stack-walk workaround changes shared print_figure error handling and deprecation timing; compatibility across supported versions requires review.
Hexbin log normalization and marginal bin behavior change without a linear-scale marginal test; the reviewer requested that missing case.
The legend handler changes color selection logic and fallback behavior; review asked whether additional affected cases needed tests.
A single accessor reads the Figure already attached to GridSpec rather than reaching it through a cell; review approved the narrowly scoped correction.
Scatter color shape handling changes a documented special case and error paths; review raised ambiguity over the array form to support.
Only titles are added to a gallery example; the later discussion concerns style preference and the plotted data remains unchanged.
Seven runnable examples are migrated from pyplot state to object methods, including event handlers; visual and interactive parity needs review.
This changes CI dependency exclusions and marks backend tests as expected failures, potentially hiding regressions; human verification of the test policy is needed.
Parallelizing all test targets with pytest-xdist changes test isolation and coverage collection; review raised an unresolved CI setup question.
The heatmap colormap copy now sets under, over, and bad colors, changing visual output for out-of-range and missing data.
The sharex and sharey conditions invert behavior for false values and may hide axis labels, a regression identified by review.
Only a malformed Sphinx role in one tutorial notebook is corrected; the executable notebook cells and runtime code do not change.
Warning cleanup spans plotting, grouping and tests across ten files; changes to observed grouping and uniqueness can alter results.
The null-data conversion path now drops values and reconstructs indexes, affecting plot alignment and Pandas compatibility.
A short contribution-guide section explains how to upgrade pip and setuptools; there is no executable or policy change.
Replacing the default request timeout with 1000 seconds changes behavior for every caller and can break long-running requests.
Preserving attributes by default changes the public result of grouping and resampling operations and requires a compatibility decision.
Removing dependency-version branches changes Dask and NumPy execution behavior for installations at the declared minimum versions.
The Sphinx build now relies on CONDA_EXE and changes generated file handling, so Windows and non-Conda documentation builds need validation.
The diff adds only future annotations to one utility module; the executable functions and their control flow remain unchanged.
Backend typing edits span twelve files and include test changes; overload and file-object compatibility need human API review.
The region-write filter excludes coordinate variables and can mishandle nondimension coordinates; reviewers requested a behavior decision first.
Adding Python 3.12 CI matrices and separate dependency environments changes what release checks execute, requiring CI validation.
The added return exits an existing fast path after its work is complete, avoiding unnecessary alignment work without changing public inputs.
Adding type checking to groupby tests exposed incompatible array conversions discussed in review; this snapshot is not ready for unattended approval.
Renaming Dataset.to_array throughout code and docs changes a public method used by downstream callers; compatibility needs human approval.
Removing the global single-threaded Dask setting changes concurrency assumptions for the entire test suite and can expose nondeterminism.
DatasetView.map now copies variable and dataset attributes under keep_attrs; this changes public metadata behavior and requires review.
Only obsolete type-ignore comments are removed from two unchanged expressions; neither runtime execution nor API shape changes.
Changing groupby alignment from outer to right alters data selection and result shape; review noted an existing test expectation was wrong.
Eagerly loading and dropping nulls before plotting can change line plots and Dask memory use; review explicitly limited the change to scatter.
The indexing adapter now handles duck Dask arrays, changing array dispatch and Pint test behavior across backends.
One documentation ecosystem link is replaced with a more current extension; no code, build logic or policy changes.
The dependency support policy is widened and minimum package versions change across setup, CI, and documentation, affecting compatibility.
MultiIndex drop_vars behavior changes from an exception to implicit removal with a deprecation warning, a public API decision.
The new hasattr guard prevents a scalar crash but the reviewer found uncertainty about which attrs are copied for Dataset inputs.
An automation workflow now installs new tools and runs a new linter-version sync script, changing bot-authored code updates.
Renaming reset_encoding while retaining wrappers changes a public method and warning behavior; review requested API documentation.
The performance shortcut iterates private coordinate names and triggered ordering failures in tests, so the snapshot needs correction.
The new real and imag properties use a replacement helper despite changing dtype, a type and behavior mismatch identified in review.
The version compatibility error handling changes and a reviewer found a missing f-string, so the intended message will not interpolate.
The test-policy update replaces an expected failure with an unconditional skip and changes pytest minimum/version flags.
The rolling exponential mean now preserves attributes by default, a public output behavior change requiring compatibility review.
The CI dependency checker swaps subprocess calls for conda.api, changing how dependency metadata is resolved and requiring CI proof.
The packaging migration removes versioneer and changes setup and generated version files; wheel and source release behavior need review.
Mypy configuration and ignores change, including a semantic config change identified by review; the quality gate needs human verification.
DataArray formatting now delegates to arbitrary array backends, changing string output and possible backend side effects.
The two file-mtime checks now expand a leading tilde consistently with file opening; no path outside this input case changes.
The array repr algorithm changes truncation output; tests even expect two ellipses in one case, which review rejected as confusing.
The change corrects spelling in docs, example comments and explanatory prose; no executable statement or API behavior changes.
Deprecating cdms2 conversion emits user warnings and skips tests on newer NumPy/Python, a public compatibility and maintenance decision.
Removing cdms2 support changes public conversion APIs and CI dependency coverage across many files; the removal policy needs human approval.
The template swaps Closes for Fixes and adds one release-note entry; GitHub issue linkage still works and no code path changes.
Only a datetime-calendar test fixture is simplified while preserving its assertion; the runtime library and public contract are unchanged.
The unused-variable checker now treats For parents like assignments, changing lint diagnostics and warranting regression review.
Pre-commit hook versions include an alpha major release; automatic formatting and CI behavior can change across the repository.
The comment workflow introduces an intentional failing step and conditional summary logic; review questioned whether the failure check works.
The suppression checker changes how ignored line-too-long messages are recorded, affecting user diagnostics and requiring regression validation.
The CI command now runs only the pylint pre-commit hook rather than all hooks, an accidental coverage reduction identified in review.
Several pre-commit hooks receive major upgrades, which change validation behavior; review identified an additional missing update.
The Python 3 checker changes when zip arguments trigger a diagnostic, so false-positive and true-positive behavior needs regression review.
Configuration enable/disable ordering changes documented public semantics, including inline and command-line cases; human policy review is required.
The used-before-assignment checker adds scope inference and new diagnostics across branches, which can produce false positives.
The CLI changes sys.path sanitization, a security-sensitive import boundary where mistaken filtering could execute unwanted code.
Only assertion messages in documentation tests are expanded; pass/fail conditions and product behavior remain identical.
The missing-return-doc checker now skips names matching a regex option, changing which diagnostics users receive.
The ignore-pattern expansion changes path handling for dot directories; exclusion behavior can expose or skip code unexpectedly.
The diff reorganizes contributor installation and testing instructions without modifying package or CI execution.
The mypy pre-commit hook and test pin upgrade together, changing the type-checking gate for the repository.
Enum member inference now discards __slots__, which changes class-checker diagnostics and deserves a regression review.
The minimum dill dependency jumps for all installations to avoid Python 3.11 hangs, a packaging compatibility decision.
The Sphinx pin jumps from 4.5 to 5.0, a major documentation build dependency change that needs a successful build.
The new stale workflow can automatically close contributor issues and PRs; maintainers questioned that policy in review.
The astroid dependency floor and CI Python support change; review specifically warned the proposed floor was not yet released.
A release-branch update changes version date and many release artifacts; release publication and provenance require human approval.
The variable checker traverses named expressions differently to change diagnostics; branch and scope edge cases require review.
The checker adds Python 3.12 generic-type scope handling, affecting undefined-variable and unused-argument diagnostics.
Pyreverse annotation formatting logic changes and the reviewer reported a genuine pre-commit failure at this snapshot.
Primer package URLs and comment links change, and review requested corrections before the tool output is reliable.
A broad cleanup of the variable checker changes imports and internal complexity across a high-impact diagnostic module.
Configuration parser internals are restructured for speed; option ordering and defaults require behavioral equivalence review.
The workflow switches to a pre-authenticated GitHub context for Primer PRs, changing token use and permissions.
Only explanatory documentation for syntax-error diagnostics is added; checker behavior and CI configuration are untouched.
Exception-handler assignment inference changes, and review requested changes because the consume implementation was uncertain.
A major mypy upgrade changes the type-checking gate and may produce new diagnostics or hide old ones.
The setuptools build floor changes substantially, while review questioned the inconsistent Python-version limit in test requirements.
The checker crash fix changes assignment inference, but review questioned whether a missing parent can still crash this path.
Only fixture files and tests for Primer comment output are added; production code and workflow behavior do not change.
The minimum test-environment setuptools version jumps by years and a reviewer requested changes to the pin.
Pre-commit hooks are updated including an alpha major release; automatic formatting and checks need validation.
A single maintainer link is added to Tidelift documentation with no runtime, build or policy logic change.
Multiple pre-commit hook versions change, including beta formatting behavior that can alter the repository quality gate.
Assertion failure formatting changes and a reviewer found truncated non-verbose output became worse for local users.
The addini typing and docstring now mention an already supported string option; runtime parsing is unchanged.
Pdb exception handling changes for SkipTest, and review requested the missing test that ordinary test-level skips still enter pdb.
The backport switches typing-only Self imports for Python 3.9 compatibility; it does not change executable control flow.
Changing assertion-rewrite cache timestamps to nanoseconds affects pyc invalidation and portability; tests and changelog needed review.
The rootdir resolution semantics for -c were wrong in the snapshot, and the reviewer requested a different approach.
pytest.approx now coerces inputs to NumPy arrays, changing comparison and optional dependency behavior; review requested more tests.
The terminal reporter changes a callback signature but setprocessor still passes the removed tags argument, a concrete failure identified in review.
The release-branch backport changes documentation references and minimum pluggy version, so the maintained branch build needs review.
The pytester fixture now uses node.name instead of function name across several paths; reviewer questioned whether this fallback is valid for all node types.
CaptureResult changes back to a namedtuple, affecting public tuple behavior and typing compatibility; consumers need regression review.
Only a deprecation test switches from a custom warning helper to pytest.warns while retaining the same warning assertions.
The Binder postBuild safety guard is replaced with REPO_DIR; if the environment marker is absent or spoofed, the script may run destructive commands.
A gallery example replaces deprecated contour handles with explicit Line2D legend handles; the reviewer confirmed the narrowly scoped visual fix.
The user guide changes shape notation from brackets to tuples without changing an API, runnable example, or build setting.
Nightly CI enables float32 tests but only on some jobs, and review noted incomplete platform coverage of the intended check.
The documentation CSS forces dropdown alignment; a reviewer could not reproduce the reported clipping across browsers and questioned the change.
Maintainer release instructions now prescribe rebase and backport steps; an incorrect sequence could corrupt the release branch.
The new release-note entry uses malformed Sphinx roles and inaccurate metric descriptions, risking broken docs and misleading public release information.
The PCA MLE dimension calculation changes numerical likelihood logic and small-eigenvalue handling, requiring scientific correctness review.
The docs upgrade changes sphinx-design minimum, JavaScript behavior, styles and lockfiles, so rendered interaction needs verification.
The linter workflow and bot comment generator change what gets displayed after CI; workflow and output behavior need review.
Cython tree internals replace C doubles with typedefs across many files; ABI and numerical behavior require careful review.
Only MinCovDet documentation is expanded and its numpydoc exemption removed; estimator computation and public signatures stay unchanged.
The minimum pandas test dependency rises and could reduce compatibility coverage for users on older supported versions.
A single sentence in an example docstring changes demoed to demonstrated; executable plotting code is identical.
The data generator now preallocates output, and review asked whether a fixed random state still produces identical shuffling.
available_if changes exception chaining and public error text, which clients and tests may inspect; compatibility needs review.
A large 1.6 changelog forward-port removes fragments and changes release documentation, requiring maintainer release validation.
Only tests replace variable random seeds with the existing global seed fixture to improve determinism; library code is untouched.
The documentation hosting trigger adds a GitHub API fallback for fork branches, changing CI publication routing and API rate-limit use.
Duplicate words are corrected across documentation and example prose; no library behavior or CI rule changes.
make_classification gains parameter validation for a public generator, changing accepted inputs and exception behavior.
roc_curve gains validation rules, and review found the proposed sparse-matrix acceptance conflicts with actual target parsing.
The user guide corrects explanatory wording around the F-measure; neither the metric implementation nor an example changes.
Multiple runnable release examples replace removed plotting APIs, so visual output and execution across versions need verification.
Changing the equality threshold in AffinityPropagation alters cluster assignment for tied points, a scientific behavior change.
HDBSCAN deprecated algorithm aliases and warning tests are removed for 1.6, changing user-facing compatibility behavior.
Encoders gain feature-name and feature-count state and validation while an older error test is removed; public fit/transform behavior changes.
Only regression tests set explicit random_state values; production multioutput code and test assertions stay the same.
KernelPCA eigenvalue filtering changes for float32 and float64, affecting numerical rank and component selection.
The documentation CI script filters towncrier fragments and computes version paths, changing which rendered pages are rebuilt.
check_array starts warning on np.matrix with planned removal, changing public validation and warning behavior.
Release notes add features to the 1.1.1 section that a reviewer said were not part of 1.1.0, requiring version accuracy review.
Windows CI coverage is disabled, removing platform-specific coverage signal as a test policy decision.
The Black formatter version changes in pre-commit and Azure CI, affecting generated formatting and quality gates.
Only notebook cell markers replace comment separators in one example; the executable statements remain identical and review comments are stylistic.
